messages:
Lina: quick pulse 1 RFC follow-up: should SDKs expose transport selection (auto/http/stream) in the public ctor, or keep it opaque and auto-chosen? leaning opaque by default.
Ravi: hide by default. most users want "just work" semantics. expose an escape hatch for power users.
Marta: agree on hide, but strong ask for debuggability. operators need to know why a request used a fallback stream vs http.
Lina: proposal: default=auto (opaque). add a debug flag: Client(..., debugTransport=true) that logs chosen transport + rationale. also surface transport decisions in Console telemetry.
Oleg: ergonomics across languages: exposing an enum in Go/TS is fine; in Python an enum arg is awkward. suggestion: accept str or enum in Python, keep typed enums in Go/TS.
Sam: code sketch for ergonomics:
```
// TS/Go-style typed
const Transport = { Auto: 'auto', Http: 'http', Stream: 'stream' }
client = new Client({ transport: Transport.Auto })

# Python-friendly
client = Client(transport='auto')  # or transport=Transport.Auto
```
Marta: second question: pagination + retry semantics. If a page request fails and is retried, do iterators return duplicate items, or resume cleanly from server cursor? need clear guarantee.
Ravi: we previously favored transparent retries for idempotent page fetches. new ask: define stronger contract.
Lina: proposed contract: provide two iterator types: Pageable (server page tokens) and Stream (continuous events). Pageable: SDK guarantees within-a-session no duplicates after transparent retries and will resume from server-provided token. Stream: best-effort de-dup, relies on server ids for exactness.
Oleg: de-dupe implementation note: for Pageable we can track item ids per session and drop repeats. but that requires stable ids from server. if ids missing, fall back to content-hash heuristic and warn.
Sam: recommend SDK expose a .resume() API that returns an opaque resume_token string which clients can persist. do NOT expose internals of token.
Marta: +1 on opaque token. that avoids coupling and allows server to evolve token shape. token is base64(json) but SDK treats it opaque.
Lina: retry/backoff policy interplay with page size: large pages need larger timeouts and different retry budgets. proposal: timeout = baseTimeout * sqrt(requested_items) and defaultMaxRetries = 3. allow per-call override.
Ravi: pluggable RetryPolicy API for advanced users. TS/Python: pass a policy object; Go: implement RetryPolicy interface with ShouldRetry(err) and NextBackoff(attempt).
Sam: sample shape:
```
// JS/Python-like simple policy object
{ maxRetries: 3, baseDelayMs: 100, jitter: true, retryableCodes: ['ECONNRESET', 503] }
```
Oleg: important compatibility note: keep default policy stable. if we tweak defaults later, ship new named policy (e.g. RetryPolicyV2) and do NOT change global defaults without major bump.
Marta: test plan: cross-lang interop tests that inject mid-page failures, simulate server-side resume tokens, and assert no duplicates for Pageable; stream tests assert best-effort semantics. I'll draft test matrix with permutations of page_size, retry_budget, and transport failure patterns.
infra-bot: queued: job/sdks/interop/retry-pagination-matrix (matrix id 3421)
Lina: UX detail: iterator surface should not expose page_token on each iteration. hide token internals; only expose .resume() returning opaque string. also add .transport_diagnostics() when debugTransport=true.
Ravi: logging: when debugTransport enabled, include chosen transport, fallback_reason, and routing decision (region/capacity-tier). redact tokens/PII.
Oleg: implementation note for Go: expose two concrete types that implement a common Iterator interface: PageablePager and EventStreamReceiver. This keeps type safety and clear API boundaries.
Sam: docs: two short patterns: "durable consumption" -> Pageable + persist resume token + server ids; "low-latency events" -> Stream + small buffer + idempotent handlers.
Marta: follow-ups: I'll write interop tests and an SDK compliance checklist. Lina, can you update RFC with API sketches and these rules?
Lina: will do. I'll add a small compatibility appendix: opaque tokens, stable defaults, opt-in advanced flags, and debug telemetry. aiming to land RFC update tomorrow and follow with SDK stubs next sprint. :rocket:
